title: Calculus for AI
notes: Hand-authored demo slice. prereqs.weight = how load-bearing (0..1). encompasses.credit = implicit repetition credit (0.2..0.4) per FIRe. Must remain a DAG. goal_tags marks the goal paths a node lies on; ['gradient-descent'] means the node is the target or an ancestor of it. blame_hint is prompt-only disambiguation for the diagnosis call, not user-facing; broad titles attract blame that belongs to other nodes.

nodes.title: Distributing a negative across a sum or difference
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for distributing a negative across a bracket, as in -(3x-2) = -3x+2. Not for sign errors in general.

nodes.title: Adding and simplifying rational expressions
nodes.blame_hint: Combining, subtracting or simplifying rational expressions. A pure numeric slip inside one is not this node: blame the topic the problem is tagged to.

nodes.title: Laws of exponents, including negative and fractional
nodes.blame_hint: Arithmetic and laws of exponents, including computing a decremented exponent wrongly, such as -3 - 1 = -4. Not for misapplying the power rule itself, which is der.power-rule.

nodes.title: Factoring polynomials
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for failing to factor a polynomial correctly. Factoring in order to resolve a 0/0 limit belongs to lim.indeterminate-factoring.

nodes.title: Solving linear and quadratic equations
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for solving a given equation wrongly. Setting up the WRONG equation, including writing the wrong f'(x) = 0, belongs to the topic that produced it.

nodes.title: Recognizing and decomposing f(g(x))
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for failing to see or decompose f(g(x)) outside of differentiation. Misidentifying inner and outer WHILE differentiating belongs to der.chain-rule.

nodes.title: Vector notation, scalar multiples and the dot product
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for vector mechanics: components, scalar multiples, subtraction, and the dot product. The direction the gradient points belongs to mv.gradient, and the descent update to ai.gradient-descent-step.

nodes.title: Converting between radicals and rational exponents
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for converting between radical and rational-exponent form. Exponent arithmetic itself belongs to alg.exponent-rules.

nodes.title: Exact values of sine and cosine at standard angles
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for wrong exact values of sine or cosine at standard angles. The derivative formulas belong to der.trig-derivatives.

nodes.title: Pythagorean and double-angle identities
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for misusing a Pythagorean or double-angle identity. A wrong angle VALUE belongs to trig.unit-circle.

nodes.title: Properties of exponentials and logarithms
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for log and exponential algebra, such as ln(ab) or e^(a+b). The derivative formulas for e^x and ln x belong to der.exp-log-derivatives.

nodes.title: Informal idea of a limit
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for not understanding what a limit is. Not for failing to evaluate one.

nodes.title: Evaluating limits by direct substitution
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for substituting incorrectly, or substituting into an undefined expression and stopping there. Reaching 0/0 and not knowing to factor belongs to lim.indeterminate-factoring, and not knowing what a limit is belongs to lim.concept.

nodes.title: Resolving 0/0 limits by factoring and cancelling
nodes.blame_hint: Reaching 0/0 and not knowing to factor and cancel, including calling it 'does not exist'.

nodes.title: Continuity at a point
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for the continuity test at a point and its three conditions. Evaluating the limit belongs to lim.direct-substitution and the meaning of a limit to lim.concept.

nodes.title: The derivative as a limit of the difference quotient
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for the difference-quotient limit itself: a malformed quotient, a dropped limit, or failing to cancel h. If the student used a shortcut rule and applied it wrongly, blame that rule's node, not this one.

nodes.title: Derivative as slope of the tangent line
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for the MEANING of f'(a) as a tangent slope, including reporting f(a) when f'(a) was asked for. Computing the derivative belongs to the rule used.

nodes.title: Power rule
nodes.blame_hint: Applying the rule itself. Exponent arithmetic errors belong to alg.exponent-rules.

nodes.title: Constant multiple and sum rules
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for the sum and constant-multiple rules: a dropped coefficient, or a constant differentiated to something other than zero. Products belong to der.product-rule and quotients to der.quotient-rule.

nodes.title: Derivatives of sine, cosine and tangent
nodes.blame_hint: The derivative formulas for sin, cos, tan. Wrong VALUES at standard angles belong to trig.unit-circle.

nodes.title: Derivatives of e^x and ln x
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for the derivative formulas of e^x and ln x. Log and exponent algebra belongs to explog.rules, and a missing inner derivative to der.chain-rule.

nodes.title: Product rule
nodes.blame_hint: Misapplying the product rule, including treating d(uv) as (du)(dv).

nodes.title: Quotient rule
nodes.blame_hint: The form of the rule itself, such as reversed numerator terms. Sign slips while expanding belong to alg.sign-distribution.

nodes.title: Chain rule
nodes.blame_hint: Failing to multiply by the derivative of the inner function, or misidentifying inner and outer.

nodes.title: Implicit differentiation
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for implicit differentiation as such, above all omitting dy/dx on a y term. A plain chain rule error belongs to der.chain-rule and the final rearrangement to alg.solving-equations.

nodes.title: Second and higher derivatives
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for taking the further derivative: stopping at the first, or misreading the order asked for. An error inside any single differentiation belongs to that rule's node.

nodes.title: Functions of several variables
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for reading or evaluating f(x,y), including confusing a variable with a parameter. Differentiating it belongs to mv.partial-derivative.

nodes.title: Partial derivatives
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for the partial derivative itself, above all differentiating with respect to BOTH variables instead of holding the others constant. An error inside the single-variable differentiation belongs to the rule used, not here.

nodes.title: Multivariable chain rule
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for the multivariable chain rule, such as omitting one path in df/dt = sum over variables of partial times derivative. A single-variable chain rule error belongs to der.chain-rule.

nodes.title: The gradient vector
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for assembling the gradient vector from its partials: wrong ordering, missing component, or returning a scalar. One partial computed wrongly belongs to mv.partial-derivative; the update that consumes the gradient belongs to ai.gradient-descent-step.

nodes.title: Directional derivatives and steepest descent
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for the directional derivative as the gradient dotted with a unit direction, including forgetting to normalise the direction. The SIGN or form of the gradient descent update belongs to ai.gradient-descent-step, never here, despite the words 'steepest descent' in the title.

nodes.title: Finding critical points
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for the procedure of setting f'(x) = 0 and locating the points. An algebra slip while solving belongs to alg.solving-equations; a differentiation slip belongs to the rule used.

nodes.title: Classifying local minima and maxima
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for classifying an already-found critical point as a minimum, maximum or neither. Moving in the wrong direction during a parameter update belongs to ai.gradient-descent-step.

nodes.title: Loss as a function of parameters
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for treating the loss as a function of the PARAMETERS rather than of the data. Not a general bucket for anything machine-learning flavoured.

nodes.title: Gradient of a loss with respect to parameters
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for computing dL/dw itself: a missing parameter, a dropped chain rule factor, or differentiating with respect to the data instead of the parameters. The update rule that consumes the gradient belongs to ai.gradient-descent-step.

nodes.title: The gradient descent update step
nodes.blame_hint: The update rule, including that it SUBTRACTS the learning rate times the gradient in order to descend.

nodes.title: Backpropagation as repeated chain rule
nodes.blame_hint: ONLY for propagating gradients layer by layer, such as skipping a layer's local derivative. The multivariable chain rule itself belongs to mv.chain-rule-multivar.
